sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. As we get older, many of us notice our sense of hearing getting worse.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔,我是乔治,我们长大了 很多人注意到我们听力越来越差

sentences.en: Maybe we need to concentrate harder or ask people to speak more loudly.
sentences.zh: 也许我们需要更集中 或要求人们 更大声说话。

sentences.en: Has that happened to you, Neil? Not really.
sentences.zh: 尼尔,你有没有这样过?

sentences.en: A while ago I thought maybe my ears were getting worse, but I had a check-up and everything was fine, thankfully.
sentences.zh: 刚才我还以为耳朵会变坏 但我做了个检查 一切都很好 幸好

sentences.en: Oh, that's great! In the UK alone, hearing loss affects 18 million people and that number is increasing.
sentences.zh: 哦 太好了 仅在英国 听力损失影响到1800万人

sentences.en: In this programme, we'll discover why we lose hearing with age and, as usual, learn some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 在这个节目中,我们会发现 为什么我们失去听力 与往常一样,学习一些有用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And you can also find a transcript of this episode on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 你也可以在我们的网站上找到这集的笔录,bbclearingenglish.com。

sentences.en: But now listen up, Georgie, because I have a question for you!
sentences.zh: 听好了,乔治,我有一个问题要问你!

sentences.en: Did you know that the three smallest bones in the human body – the hammer, the anvil, and the stirrup – are all located in the ear?
sentences.zh: 你知不知道人的身体的三个最小的骨头——锤子、子和子——都放在耳朵里?

sentences.en: But which one of those is the smallest? Is it: a) the hammer, b) the anvil, or c) the stirrup bone?
sentences.zh: 究竟哪个是最小的呢?是锤子,b),或c)骨呢?

sentences.en: Hmm. That one's a difficult one. I'm going to say the anvil bone.
sentences.zh: 嗯,那一个很难,我要说那根刺骨

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the answer later on.
sentences.zh: 好吧,我们晚点再找出答案

sentences.en: To understand why our hearing gets worse with age, it's useful to know a little about how the ear works in the first place.
sentences.zh: 为了理解为什么我们的听力会随着年龄而恶化, 了解一下耳朵是如何工作的,是非常有用的。

sentences.en: Here's Mr Nish Mehta, an ear, nose and throat surgeon at Royal National ENT Hospital in London, giving a beginners' class to BBC Radio 4 programme, Inside Health: Hearing is an amazing sense.
sentences.zh: Nish Mehta先生是伦敦皇家ENT医院的耳鼻喉外科医生,

sentences.en: It's a special sense, and the ear is really the hearing organ.
sentences.zh: 这是一种特殊的感官 耳朵真的是听力器官

sentences.en: So, the ear is split up into three main parts: there's the outer ear, the middle ear and the inner ear.
sentences.zh: 因此,耳朵被分成三个主要部分: 外耳,中耳和内耳。

sentences.en: The outer ear is the bit that you see – it's on the side of your head.
sentences.zh: 外耳是被你看到的部分 - 在你的头上。

sentences.en: We call that the pinna. Think of that as the satellite dish.
sentences.zh: 我们称它为pinna 把它当做卫星天线

sentences.en: It collects the sounds and it funnels them in towards the sense organ.
sentences.zh: 它收集声音 并把它们输送到感官器官。

sentences.en: That then gets transmitted to the middle ear.
sentences.zh: 然后传到中耳

sentences.en: The middle ear's main job is to amplify those sounds.
sentences.zh: 中间耳朵的主要工作 是放大这些声音。

sentences.en: That's done by having an eardrum, which catches it and then vibrates sympathetically to the vibration of the noise that you heard.
sentences.zh: 这是通过有一个耳膜, 它抓住它,然后振动 同情的振动 你听到的噪音。

sentences.en: And then that's passed on to the three smallest bones in the body: the hammer, the anvil and the stirrup.
sentences.zh: 然后传到身体上三个最小的骨头上: 锤子、子和子。

sentences.en: The ear is made up of outer, middle and inner parts.
sentences.zh: 耳朵由外部、中部和内部组成。

sentences.en: It's one of our sense organs: specific parts of the body – your ears, eyes, tongue, nose and skin – which allow you to experience the outside world.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的感官器官之一:身体的具体部分——你的耳朵、眼睛、舌头、鼻子和皮肤——使你能够体验外部世界。

sentences.en: The visible part – the outer ear or pinna – acts like a satellite dish, collecting sounds which it funnels into the middle ear.
sentences.zh: 可见的部分——外耳或外针——表现得像卫星天线,收集声音,将声音传入中耳。

sentences.en: The verb funnel means to move or direct something through a narrow space.
sentences.zh: 动词漏斗意味着 移动或引导的东西 通过一个狭窄的空间。

sentences.en: Once in the middle ear, the eardrum amplifies the sounds before transmitting them to tiny hairs in the inner ear, which then sends electrical signals to the brain.
sentences.zh: 一旦进入中耳 耳膜会放大声音 然后再传到内耳的小毛上 然后向大脑发出电子信号

sentences.en: It's an incredible system, but unfortunately one that can go wrong at any stage.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人难以置信的系统, 但不幸的是,它可以在任何阶段出错。

sentences.en: Here, James Gallagher, presenter of BBC Radio 4's Inside Health, asks Nish Mehta when problems tend to start.
sentences.zh: 英国广播公司第四电台《内部健康》的主持人James Gallagher问Nish Mehta问题什么时候开始。

sentences.en: We're going to spend a lot of today, Nish, thinking about age-related hearing loss.
sentences.zh: 我们今天要花很多时间去思考 与年龄有关的听力损失

sentences.en: When does that start? Wear and tear of your hearing starts from around the age of eight.
sentences.zh: 什么时候开始的?

sentences.en: OK? OK. So, we're doomed already! We're already on a downward spiral, but we've got a lot of redundancy in the system.
sentences.zh: 好了,我们完蛋了,我们已经在螺旋式下降了,但系统里有很多冗余。

sentences.en: And the speed at which our hearing declines is partly based on the genetics that you're born with and then partly based on the environment that you're exposed to.
sentences.zh: 我们听力下降的速度 部分基于你所生的基因 部分基于你所接触的环境

sentences.en: So, someone who has really strong genetics to protect them from hearing, but spends their life on a pneumatic drill, may have a much faster decline than someone on the other side.
sentences.zh: 所以,一个有很强的遗传学 来保护他们不受听觉伤害的人, 却把一生花在充气钻上的人, 可能比另一边的人下降得更快。

sentences.en: You can imagine that your brain is doing so much computation behind the scenes just to listen to someone speaking and understand the words they are saying.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象你的大脑在幕后做了这么多的计算 只是为了听别人说话 听懂他们说的话

sentences.en: So, whilst hearing is going, the brain tends to increase its listening effort, and so often it's a very slow process for you to realise that you're struggling with hearing.
sentences.zh: 所以,在听力发展的时候, 大脑倾向于增加它的听力, 并且经常是一个非常缓慢的过程 让你意识到你正在挣扎着听力。

sentences.en: Wear and tear of our hearing starts as young as eight.
sentences.zh: 我们的听力从小到八岁就开始了

sentences.en: Wear and tear means the damage that comes from ordinary, everyday use.
sentences.zh: 穿戴和撕裂意味着普通的日常使用所造成的破坏。

sentences.en: When Nish says this, James exclaims, " We're doomed!" – an informal way of saying we're destined to fail.
sentences.zh: 当尼什这样说时,詹姆斯就说,“我们注定要失败了!” 一种非正式的说法。

sentences.en: From the age of eight our hearing is on a downward spiral – a situation which gets worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 从八岁开始,我们的听力在下降,情况越来越糟。

sentences.en: But don't worry just yet! Human hearing has evolved with redundancy in the system – a technical phrase meaning that there are many ways to achieve the same outcome so that a backup system can take over if other systems fail.
sentences.zh: 但不要担心!人类的听力随着系统冗余而演变 — — 一个技术性的短语意味着有许多方法可以实现同样的结果,这样如果其他系统失灵,备份系统就可以接管。

sentences.en: Here, for example, the brain works harder to compensate for a weaker sound signal reaching the inner ear.
sentences.zh: 比如说,大脑更努力地工作 来弥补内耳收到的声音信号变弱

sentences.en: And there are other ways hearing loss can be helped as well, including hearing aids, surgery or even just removing extra ear wax – not a job I would like very much!
sentences.zh: 还有其它方法可以帮助听力损失, 包括助听器、手术, 甚至只是去除额外的耳蜡,

sentences.en: After that fascinating journey into the world of hearing, I think it's time to reveal the answer to your question, Neil.
sentences.zh: 进入听力世界的奇妙旅程之后 我想是时候 揭开你问题的答案了 尼尔

sentences.en: I asked you, "Which is the smallest bone in the body?" and they are all in the ear.
sentences.zh: 我问你,"什么是最小的骨头 在身体?" 他们都在耳朵里。

sentences.en: Is it a) the hammer, b) the anvil, or c) the stirrup bone?
sentences.zh: 是锤子,b),或c)骨吗?

sentences.en: I said the anvil, didn't I? You did, but I'm afraid you obviously weren't listening in Biology class because you are wrong.
sentences.zh: 我说了Avil,不是吗?但恐怕你显然没在生物课上听 因为你错了

sentences.en: It is, in fact, the stirrup bone. Ah! OK.
sentences.zh: 事实上,是搅拌骨

sentences.en: Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with sense organs – specific parts of the body, like your ears and eyes, which allow you to experience the world.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下我们所学的词汇,从感官器官开始-- 身体的具体部分,比如你的耳朵和眼睛, 使你能够体验世界。

sentences.en: To funnel means to move or direct something through a narrow space, and a funnel, the noun, is a cone-shaped tool which does this.
sentences.zh: 漏斗意味着通过狭小的空间移动或引导某种东西, 漏斗,即名词,是一个圆锥形的工具,可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Wear and tear refers to the damage that comes from using something every day.
sentences.zh: 穿戴和撕裂是指每天使用某种东西所造成的损害。

sentences.en: If you say, " We're doomed!" you mean we're going to be defeated or fail.
sentences.zh: 如果你说"我们注定要失败了" 你是说我们会被打败或失败

sentences.en: And a downward spiral is a situation which continuously gets worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 螺旋式下降是一种情况不断恶化。

sentences.en: And finally, redundancy in the system refers to having more than one way to achieve an objective so that a backup can take over if other methods fail.
sentences.zh: 最后,系统中的冗余是指实现一个目标的不止一种方法,这样,如果其他方法失败,备份就可以接管。

sentences.en: You'll be sad to hear that, once again, our six minutes are up, but why not head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to try the quiz and worksheet for this episode.
sentences.zh: 你会难过地听到,再次, 我们的六分钟了, 但为什么不去我们的网站,bbclearingenglish.com, 尝试测试和工作表 对于这集。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now! Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见,再见
